record.original_question: Let A053392 map a decimal integer to the decimal concatenation of the sums of each pair of consecutive digits, and then remove duplicates to obtain A347520. Explain why the associated 4-regular graphs of this de-duplicated digit-concatenation sequence are so striking and highly regular.

evidence.quote: A053392 is easy to define: we write n in decimal digits, consider each pair of consecutive digits and replace them by their sum. The integer 9327, for example, would lead to (9+ 3).(3+ 2).(2+ 7) = 12.5.9 = 1259 and thus a_9327 = 1259.
Removing duplicates, we end up with the sequence under consideration – it results in a striking and highly regular graph, see Fig. 13.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a map f on positive integers as follows: write n in base 10 as a string of digits d_1 d_2 … d_k (with k ≥ 2), form the sequence of pairwise sums s_i = d_i + d_{i+1} for i = 1, …, k−1, and let f(n) be the integer whose decimal representation is the concatenation of the decimal representations of s_1, s_2, …, s_{k−1} (so each s_i contributes one or two decimal digits). For example, f(9327) = concat(9+3, 3+2, 2+7) = concat(12, 5, 9) = 1259. For 1 ≤ n ≤ 9 (single-digit n), set f(n) = 0.

Form the infinite sequence (f(1), f(2), f(3), …), and then delete repeated entries to obtain a sequence (b_1, b_2, b_3, …) in which each value appears at most once (in order of first appearance). For each integer N ≥ 1, build a graph G_N on the vertex set {1, 2, …, N} by connecting each index i (with 1 ≤ i ≤ N − 2) to the indices i+1 and i+2 (so that, away from the two endpoints, every vertex has degree 4); then label vertex i by the value b_i, and embed the graph in the plane by placing vertex i at a position whose coordinates are determined by b_i (for instance, at (i, b_i) or by a similar coordinate scheme derived from b_i).

Provide a rigorous mathematical explanation of why the resulting 4-regular planar drawings exhibit the strikingly regular geometric patterns observed: identify the arithmetic or combinatorial properties of the de-duplicated digit-pair-sum sequence (b_n) responsible for these large-scale regularities, and quantify them (for example, by describing the asymptotic distribution of b_n, the recurring linear/affine substructures formed by the visible "rays" or "bands," and their slopes and densities).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a problem list on finding structure in integer sequences via graph theory, where it is posed informally without resolution. No subsequent work explaining the regular structure of the de-duplicated digit-pair-sum graphs was located in the search.
